PullRequest.Title: chat: Add continuous customization discovery paging
PullRequest.Body:
## Before

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a1a8c56-4a19-4edc-94b9-a4347bf454e5)

## After

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f952bf1-0050-41d0-9977-e8d57d709431)

## Summary
- remove the manual Load More fallback from customization Discover results
- continuously request cursor pages near the list boundary and while filtered results underfill the viewport
- preserve loaded rows, cancellation, retries, source changes, and expose loading through polite announcements and `aria-busy`
- expand paging tests and keep loading fixtures synchronized with scheduled continuation

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationDiscoveryPage.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationDiscoveryPage.test.ts src\vs\workbench\test\browser\componentFixtures\sessions\aiCustomizationManagementEditor.fixture.ts`
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationDiscoveryPage.test.ts` (22 passing)
- `npx component-explorer render -p .\test\componentFixtures\component-explorer.json --fixture-id-regex 'chat/aiCustomizations/aiCustomizationManagementEditor/Discover(InfiniteScroll|Loading)/(Dark|Light)' --timeout 120000` (4 fixtures passed)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added scheduler call, `layout()` call after every request completion, local eight-page loop, test expecting an automatic ninth request, and marketplace implementation's IPC/HTTPS query path establish the mechanism directly. Exact catalog depth and network latency vary, which affects severity rather than causality.
Findings.PerformanceResource: sequential marketplace IPC calls, HTTPS requests, response bytes, and accumulated catalog objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the number of remote catalog pages before enough locally matching rows fill the viewport, or with the entire result depth when no matching type exists; each scheduled invocation permits another batch of up to 8 pages, with no search-wide cap.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive network I/O and prolonged search loading
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The same filtered search stopped automatically after at most 8 pages and rendered a `Load More` button, so further network requests required explicit user action. The PR removes that fallback and automatically requests page 9 and subsequent batches.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Underfilled or near-bottom search results now automatically schedule another continuation batch after each render; because the eight-page counter is local to each `loadCatalog` call, automatic scheduling repeatedly resets the counter and keeps fetching until a matching list fills the viewport or the catalog is exhausted.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `this.continuationScheduler.schedule()` at `aiCustomizationDiscoveryPage.ts:1095` runs from `layout()` after every completed render while the list is underfilled. Each scheduled `loadCatalog(true)` resets the local `pageCount` loop and can issue another `maxFilteredCatalogPagesPerLoad` (8) marketplace queries. The updated test explicitly proves the behavior crosses the former bound by expecting request 9 without a click.
Findings.Title: Bound automatic continuation across the whole search
Findings.Impact: A search such as `@type:plugin mail` with sparse plugin matches can silently walk the entire remote result set, keeping Discover busy and generating many sequential IPC/HTTPS requests even though the user did not request more pages. On a large or slow catalog this causes prolonged background loading, excess bandwidth/server traffic, and increasing CPU/allocation as all pages are accumulated and re-filtered.
Findings.Evidence: `loadCatalog` invokes `marketplaceService.query` sequentially up to 8 times for filtered plugin searches where no single server media type exists. Each marketplace query crosses shared-process IPC on desktop and `AgentFinderRestProvider.query` performs a cancellable HTTPS request (potentially more while skipping unsupported pages). `render()` calls `layout()`, which reaches the added scheduler line and launches another 8-query batch when filtered rows still do not fill the viewport. `catalogPage.items` also accumulates every fetched page, so network, allocation, copying, and filtering all grow with remote result depth.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep a continuation budget across scheduler invocations for the current query/source (rather than resetting it per `loadCatalog` call), and require explicit user action or another bounded trigger after that budget is exhausted. Reset the budget only when the query/source changes; preserve cancellation and cursor ordering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type-filtered search whose matching rows are sparse or absent
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the 300 ms search delay, the first page and up to eight filtered backfill pages complete before `loadCatalog` renders. The added post-render layout check then schedules another batch immediately while results underfill the viewport, so each sequential batch is on the ongoing search-loading path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Continue the marketplace query with the opaque cursor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 8 combined-page calls per `loadCatalog` invocation; the new scheduler repeats invocations until enough locally matching rows fill the viewport or all N remote pages are exhausted. The changed test demonstrates at least a ninth call. Each desktop call crosses IPC; web uses the workbench service directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automatic work stopped after one bounded batch of at most 8 calls and further continuation required clicking `Load More`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each call must resolve before the current batch can finish and render; automatically repeated batches keep the search busy.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET/POST AgentFinder browse/search pages and parse bounded JSON responses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one HTTPS catalog request per consumed 24-item source page for the single registered AgentFinder source; provider-side skipping of unsupported-only pages can require additional requests. Automatic UI continuation now scales through all pages needed to fill the local filtered list or exhaust the catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automatic network requests beyond the existing 8-page filtered backfill; page 9+ required user action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Requests are sequential and keep search continuation active; each has a 30-second timeout and up to a 5 MiB bounded response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of remote search pages before enough resources survive local type filtering to fill the viewport; worst case is the full result depth when no resource matches the requested local type.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One UI marketplace query is active at a time because `loading` gates continuation and the backfill loop awaits each query. The regression is sequential unbounded fan-out, not concurrent burst. The marketplace may query enabled providers concurrently, but only one provider is registered today.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Nonempty searches do not use `browseCatalogCache`; the marketplace continuation LRU preserves cursor/source state but does not cache already-consumed pages. Cold and subsequent cursor pages therefore continue to cross the service boundary. Query/source changes reset state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added scheduler, post-request render/layout path, local per-call page counter, production IPC/HTTPS implementation, and updated test expecting request 9 directly prove the fan-out.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog depth, match distribution, and real network latency vary, and the source is default-off experimental. The ninth request and lack of a search-wide cap are directly established, so uncertainty lowers severity but does not weaken the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium boundary-fanout regression: automatic continuation resets the former eight-page bound and can drain the remote result set without further user input.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll near the end of a populated result list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the user scrolls within three rows of the bottom, one scheduled continuation must complete before new rows appear. Existing rows remain usable while loading.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the next marketplace cursor page after near-end scrolling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One combined-page marketplace call for ordinary searches, or up to 8 sequential calls for locally filtered plugin backfill, per accepted continuation trigger; one registered source means normally the same number of HTTPS pages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The scroll handler called `loadCatalog(true)` directly. The PR schedules it at delay zero, coalescing duplicate scroll notifications without increasing effective concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The call supplies the next visible rows and is therefore on the scroll-continuation path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the next AgentFinder search page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one HTTPS request per combined page with the current single source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary was reached directly from the scroll handler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New rows wait for the request, as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of user-reached list boundaries and locally filtered pages per boundary.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The scheduler coalesces same-turn scroll events and `loading` prevents overlapping requests. Effective continuation concurrency remains one.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Search pages are not result-cached, but the opaque continuation preserves provider buffers. Scroll events for the same current state are coalesced by one `RunOnceScheduler`; no negative-cache behavior is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: scheduler and loading guards are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual page latency varies, but changed coalescing behavior is clear.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression: delay-zero scheduling coalesces scroll notifications and preserves single-request ordering. The unbounded underfill chain is covered by the reported finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hide and reveal Discover during automatic continuation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hiding cancels the active request. Showing rerenders and the layout check schedules a replacement continuation only if the page is visible, underfilled/near-bottom, and has a cursor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resume a pending marketplace cursor after the Discover page becomes visible again.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One canceled IPC/network continuation and at most one replacement request for the same cursor on reveal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no automatic underfill scheduler to resume; user-triggered continuation was canceled on hide.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The replacement must finish to add rows after reveal; cancellation prevents hidden work from continuing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one replacement HTTPS page under the loading/cancellation guards.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automatic replacement for an underfill continuation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only continuation results wait on it; existing content remains rendered.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of hide/show transitions during an active continuation; each transition is bounded to one replacement.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cancellation is requested before the replacement is scheduled; sequence checks reject stale completion. At most one authoritative continuation advances state, though transport cancellation may briefly overlap with replacement teardown.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The current cursor and accumulated items remain in page state while hidden. No search result cache is added; showing again continues from the same cursor. Browse-mode cache is unrelated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High based on explicit cancellation, sequence checks, and the added hide/show test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Transport-level cancellation timing varies, but sequence and token guards make retained overlap bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable performance issue: cancellation and replacement are bounded and stale completions are ignored.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change query or marketplace source during paging
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A changed query waits for the existing 300 ms scheduler then starts a fresh catalog request; source selection starts immediately. Canceled stale work is off the new result publication path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel stale search and query the selected source/query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fresh IPC query after each settled query/source change, followed by cursor pages according to result fill. Rapid typing is coalesced by the existing 300 ms scheduler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same cancellation and debounce behavior; the PR additionally cancels any pending continuation scheduler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The fresh request is required for new search results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one HTTPS request for the settled initial query with the current source, plus continuation behavior described in the first scenario.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of settled query/source changes rather than keystrokes within the debounce window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cancellation plus request sequence checks prevent stale publication; only one current request is authoritative.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Query or source changes clear catalog state and cancel current requests. New nonempty searches start cold after debounce; empty browse mode can reuse `browseCatalogCache` by source key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from cancellation and scheduler code plus source/query cancellation tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: User typing cadence varies; debounce bounds rapid changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression: pending continuation is canceled and rapid search input remains coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or reveal queryless Discover browse mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cold browse waits for one initial catalog query; warm browse renders cached entries. Automatic search continuation is off this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold: one IPC query and normally one HTTPS request for 24 combined items. Warm cache: zero. Recovery or source changes invalidate and return to cold behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unchanged; added continuation checks require a nonempty query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold browse sections wait for the page; warm cached rendering does not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold versus warm page/source state, not catalog depth.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One cold browse query; no continuation scheduling for empty query.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Queryless browse pages use `browseCatalogCache` keyed by selected source; warm reveal avoids a new catalog query unless recovery/source enablement invalidates the cache. The continuation scheduler explicitly rejects empty queries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the empty-query guard and browse cache reads/writes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cache lifetime follows the page object and configured-source changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: automatic continuation excludes browse mode and existing warm-cache behavior is preserved.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files. One medium boundary-fanout regression was reported: automatic underfill continuation repeatedly resets the existing eight-page batch bound and can issue sequential IPC/HTTPS requests through the full filtered catalog. Scroll coalescing, cancellation/resume, query/source changes, browse caching, layout work, test retry polling, and fixture timing introduced no additional high-confidence performance findings.
